قَاشِبٌ [act. part. n. of قَشَبَ; Mixing: &c.]. ―
-b2- One who imputes to others, or charges them with, vices, or faults, that are in himself. (IAar, TA.) ―
-b3- And A tailor (O, K) who ejects his ↓ أَقْشَاب , i. e. the knots of the threads, [meaning who spits them out,] when he ejects them. (O.) ＝
-A2- And [A man] weak in respect of the body (ضَعِيفُ النَّفْسِ); (K, TA;) i. e. (TA) one whose قِشْب [meaning body] is weak, or emaciated; (O, TA;) by his فِشْب being meant his نَفْس [as syn. with جَسَد]. (O.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
